Congenital Heart Disease: The patient has a known complex congenital heart disease, including a single ventricle defect, double-outlet right ventricle with D-transposition of the great arteries, and an ostium secundum atrial septal defect with left superior vena cava. The recent cardiac catheterization and hemodynamic instability during the procedure are consistent with complications of congenital heart disease. The patient's symptoms, including occasional cyanosis and low oxygen saturation, are also consistent with this diagnosis.
Seizure Disorder: The patient developed clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions after the cardiac catheterization, which are consistent with seizure activity. The noncontrast head CT showed a slight diffuse increase in cortical density, which may indicate cerebral injury or edema. The recent history of cardiorespiratory arrest and the abnormal head CT findings support the diagnosis of a seizure disorder, possibly related to the cardiac procedure or underlying congenital heart disease.
